Lisa Demuth

Republican candidate for Governor & Lieutenant Governor, Minnesota · Open seat

Speaker of the Minnesota House of Representatives

Lisa Demuth, a Republican from Cold Spring, has represented District 13A in the Minnesota House since 2019 and is the current House Speaker. She announced her run for governor in November 2025 and picked Maple Grove attorney Ryan Wilson as her running mate. She won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary, beating Mike Lindell and Kendall Qualls.

Where Demuth stands

Government fraud
Proposes a Fraud Prevention Plan. She says she made an independent Office of Inspector General with law enforcement authority a top priority as Speaker and delivered it in the last session.
Government fraud
Says she would push for jail time and other penalties for people caught stealing public funds.
Taxes and affordability
Her Affordability Agenda proposes $1 billion in state savings, lower income tax rates, a $99 cap on car tabs, ending the state tax on Social Security, and property tax relief.
Public safety
Her Public Safety Plan proposes 'Three Strikes' for violent crimes, tougher penalties for fleeing police and for assaulting officers, ending open-air drug markets and homeless camps, and more funding for Violent Crime Enforcement Teams.
K-12 education
Proposes an 'Education Comeback' centered on academic results and reading proficiency. She says she would keep gender and racial ideology out of classrooms and put money into classrooms rather than administration.
Health care
Says she would keep supporting rural hospitals across party lines, offer families more health plan options, and make sure health care funds don't go to fraud or to people in the country illegally. She points to voting for insulin price caps.
Tariffs/trade
In the final debate, she said she has disagreed with President Trump on tariffs and on decisions about beef imports.
